chunks: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn b. al-Hasan b. Aban narrated to us, from al-Husayn b. Sa'id, from Fadala b. Ayyub, from Yahya al-Halabi, from his father, from Abdullah b. Sulayman, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him),

that he said to a man: O so-and-so, do not sit with the wealthy, for indeed a servant sits with them while he sees that Allah has blessed him, but he does not stand up until he believes that Allah has not blessed him at all.

key_terms.الأغنياء: al-Aghniya' - The wealthy/rich: those possessing material abundance, whose company is warned against due to the psychological effect of comparison
key_terms.العبد: al-'Abd - The servant: a human being in relation to Allah, emphasizing servitude and dependence on divine grace
key_terms.نعمة: Ni'mah - Blessing/bounty: divine favor from Allah that one risks losing sight of when comparing with the wealthy

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about sitting with the wealthy in al-Amali of Shaykh al-Saduq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (as) warns a man against sitting with the wealthy, explaining that a servant who sits with them initially recognizes Allah's blessings upon him, but by the time he leaves, he feels that Allah has not blessed him at all. This teaching addresses the psychological harm of comparing oneself to the affluent, a common theme in early Islamic ethical discourse where scholars cautioned that envy and ingratitude arise from social comparison rather than actual deprivation.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (rh) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. al-Hasan b. Aban narrated to us from al-Husayn b. Sa`id from Fadala b. Ayyub from Yahya al-Halabi from his father from `Abdullah b. Sulayman from Abi Ja`far al-Baqir (as). He said to a man: O so-and-so! Do not sit with the rich, for a servant who sits with them sees that Allah has blessed them, and he does not stand until he believes that Allah has not blessed him.
